target.title: feat(ios): resume chat from the afterSeq cursor on reconnect
target.body:
**Stacked PR**: based on the gateway branch `feat/gateway-chat-history-after-seq` (#100267) and must land after it.

Part of #100197

## What Problem This Solves

When the iOS app reconnects (foreground resume, or a detected event seq gap), it refetches the entire chat history and wholesale-replaces the timeline. On long sessions this is slow, wasteful, and can visibly churn the transcript when only a handful of messages were missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now supports an `afterSeq` catch-up cursor on `chat.history` (#100267). This PR adopts it in the shared chat pipeline: the view model tracks the highest applied transcript seq (`__openclaw.seq`), and reconnect paths fetch only the missed delta, looping `nextAfterSeq`/`hasMore` and appending through the existing reconciliation/dedup path. Delta pages are re-anchored into transcript-seq order because the gap-triggering newer push is delivered before the async delta returns. Version skew is a named contract: if the response lacks the `afterSeq` echo, the gateway ignored the cursor and the client falls back to today's full-replace path — same for fresh sessions with no tracked seq. Also fixes a latent bug where a seq gap drained pending runs but left stale streaming assistant text on screen. The post-send refresh ladder is deliberately untouched (its rungs also cover missed chat-final events); retiring rungs is a follow-up once the cursor proves out.

## User Impact

Reconnects after backgrounding or transport gaps fetch only missed messages instead of the full transcript: faster catch-up, less data, no timeline churn, and no more stale "streaming" bubble after a connection gap. Older gateways keep the exact current behavior.

## Evidence

- New `ChatHistoryAfterSeqTests` (7 tests): delta append without duplicates, multi-page cursor loop, push-before-delta ordering race, legacy full-page fallback, fresh-session full fetch, seq-gap streaming-text cleanup, foreground delta fetch.
- `swift build` + `swift test --filter ChatViewModelTests` (105/105) green in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`, post-rebase onto the final gateway head.
- Flake diligence: the one timing flake seen also reproduces on the pure base branch (2/8 runs) with the identical failure — pre-existing parallel-load flake, tracked separately.
- Contract verified against `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` on the base branch, including `attachOpenClawTranscriptMeta` seq stamping on pushed rows.
- Codex autoreview: one accepted P1 (delta appended after newer pushed rows could misorder the transcript) fixed with a regression test; final branch review clean ("patch is correct").

Known gaps: no full iOS `xcodebuild` in this environment (the app-target diff is a 12-line mirror of an adjacent compiling method; CI covers it); macOS WebChat transport intentionally stays on the legacy full-page default (identical to today) — follow-up can add its override.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gateway-backed and embedded TUI sessions could drop live assistant output when a runtime emitted incremental `delta` frames without also repeating the cumulative `text` snapshot. Users saw no progress until the final response, despite the runtime streaming correctly.

Streaming text appears incrementally in both normal Gateway TUI sessions and `tui --local`, including runtimes that emit canonical delta-only events. Commentary suppression, abort handling, buffer caps, and final-message behavior are unchanged.

target.title: fix(gateway): use account-scoped reload for channel account changes
target.body:
## Summary

Use account-scoped hot reload for config changes under:

- `channels.<channel>.accounts.<accountId>.*`

instead of always restarting the entire channel.

## What changed

- added account-scoped restart planning to `GatewayReloadPlan`
- detect account-scoped channel config paths in `buildGatewayReloadPlan`
- route those changes through:
  - `stopChannel(channelId, accountId)`
  - `startChannel(channelId, accountId)`
- preserve full channel restart behavior for:
  - channel-global config changes
  - mixed changes where full-channel restart takes precedence

## Why

The gateway reload framework already has account-scoped channel lifecycle support, but hot reload planning previously collapsed all matching channel config changes into full channel restarts.

That makes account-only config edits broader and more disruptive than necessary.

## Tests

Added coverage for:

- account-scoped channel account config -> account-only restart
- channel-global config -> full channel restart
- mixed account-scoped + channel-global changes -> full channel restart wins
- multiple account-scoped changes in one channel -> collect all impacted accounts

Validated with:

```bash
corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server.reload.test.ts
```

## Scope / non-goals

This change is intentionally narrow.

It does not redesign active reply draining, typing lifecycle coordination, or provider-specific recovery behavior.


Closes #43935

target.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default
target.body:
## Summary

Deny same-provider cross-context `message` tool sends by default. A tool call bound to one conversation can still reply to the current conversation, but sending/uploading into another conversation on the same provider now requires explicit opt-in via:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    message: {
      crossContext: {
        allowWithinProvider: true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The legacy broad `tools.message.allowCrossContextSend=true` escape hatch is preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

Cross-provider sends were already denied by default, but same-provider cross-context sends were allowed unless `allowWithinProvider` was explicitly set to `false`. That permissive default makes it too easy for work/approval in one Discord thread to accidentally drive an externally visible message send into another thread on the same provider.

This PR makes current-conversation delivery the safe default while preserving an explicit compatibility opt-in for installations that intentionally bridge conversations.

## Duplicate / overlap check

I checked upstream issues/PRs and local source for exact overlap before opening this PR. I did not find an exact duplicate for changing the same-provider cross-context default.

Adjacent but not duplicate:

- #74799: per-session runtime envelopes; useful substrate, but not this default policy change.
- #91800: external content provenance/policy-hook style; adjacent, not cross-context send authorization.
- #77442 / #88803 / #89949 / #54531: delivery route/origin persistence; adjacent routing work, not this message tool default.

## Panel review / scope revision

A 3-lane consult review recommended a narrow first PR rather than a broad runtime approval resolver. The revised scope is intentionally limited to the existing `enforceCrossContextPolicy` seam:

- no live patch / no gateway activation
- no cron/webhook changes in this PR
- no rewrite of Discord routing/session compaction
- preserve ordinary replies to the current conversation
- keep explicit config opt-in for existing cross-context workflows

## Changes

- Change `allowWithinProvider` default from permissive (`!== false`) to explicit opt-in (`=== true`).
- Update policy tests for default same-provider denial and explicit same-provider opt-in.
- Update config help text and FAQ wording to document that cross-context messaging is blocked by default, including same-provider conversation hops.

## Evidence

Latest amended/rebased head: `e0e4259e40c283f986d790686e929463628ed77f`.
Current base used for local validation: `openclaw/openclaw@2920dc32820cb2add798cbca294131a0017dbc70`.

Focused validation after fixing the broad shard failures:

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.context.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

Observed result:

```text

message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts: 11 tests passed
message-action-runner.context.test.ts: 26 tests passed
core prod tsgo: passed
core test tsgo: passed
pnpm check:test-types: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The failing broad shard cases are now covered directly:

- same-provider message-tool-only sends are denied by default before durable delivery;
- explicitly opted-in same-provider cross-context sends still preserve required durable delivery;
- dry-run UI handoff tests now assert default denial for same-provider conversation hops;
- direct/local chat mismatch cases now assert default denial while same-conversation sends remain allowed;
- current-main lint suppression allowlist drift is refreshed for the rebased tree;
- current-main `exec-policy` generic layer merge preserves `base` fields while satisfying TS boundary checks.

Earlier focused assertion check also passed in an isolated worktree:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/test-cross-context-policy.ts
# cross-context policy focused assertions passed
```

## Rollout note

This is a behavior-tightening default. Existing deployments that intentionally send to other conversations on the same provider should set `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider=true`.

target.title: fix: persist queued iOS watch replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS watch quick replies being held only in memory after the phone receives them while disconnected from the gateway. If the app process was terminated before reconnecting, those queued replies could be silently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watch quick replies now use a UserDefaults-backed queue scoped to the current gateway stable ID. Reconnect flushing peeks queued replies, forwards them through a confirmed `node.event` request, and removes them only after delivery succeeds; failed sends are left queued for a later reconnect.

## User Impact

Users can tap watch quick replies while the phone is offline and still have those replies delivered after the iOS app restarts and reconnects, without replaying stale replies into a different gateway.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(browser): bound Playwright response body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** `responseBodyViaPlaywright` calls `resp.text()` which decodes the entire response string (OOM risk on multi-MB responses).

**Solution:** Bounded-read strategy — content-length pre-reject for known-large responses, `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)` decode window for all others. Full Buffer allocation stays for non-pre-rejected responses but full-string decoding is bounded.

**What changed:**
- Content-length pre-reject: skip `resp.body()` entirely when content-length exceeds `maxBytes`, return `{ body: "", truncated: true }`
- `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)` decode window bounds string allocation
- CLI now shows explicit oversized-response notice instead of blank output
- Removed CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` path (page-delivery truncation issue)
- Unified to single `body()+subarray()` path for all browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)

**What did NOT change:** Public API, return types, existing caller behavior, browser support matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

`responseBodyViaPlaywright` previously used `resp.text()` — full JS string decode before truncation check. On a 500 MB response this allocated 500 MB+ string memory.

`resp.body()` returns a `Buffer` (Node.js native, no encoding cost). Combined with `buf.subarray(0, maxBytes)`, only the bounded prefix is decoded to string — the full 500 MB allocation becomes a 500 MB Buffer + ~800 KB string instead of a 500 MB string. For known-large responses (content-length > maxBytes), the pre-reject path avoids the Buffer entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR introduced CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` for truly bounded memory capture (no full Buffer). However, CDP intercept-at-Response-stage forces `Fetch.fulfillRequest` with the captured (truncated) body, which disrupts page network behavior — the page receives a bounded prefix instead of the original response. This is fundamental to CDP's design: once the body is taken from the stream, the original response can't be forwarded.

Removing the CDP path eliminates this class of bug entirely:
- Page always receives the original response (body, status, headers untouched)
- No CDP session management (Fetch.enable/disable, cleanup timing)
- Single code path for all browsers (simpler to maintain)
- 200 lines of CDP code deleted, 4 CDP-specific tests deleted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Bounded response-body reads — (1) content-length pre-reject, (2) body()+subarray() bounded decode, (3) CLI oversized-response message.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js 22 with Vitest, Playwright Chromium browser test harness

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
# node browser-proof.mjs  ← real Playwright Chromium, local HTTP server, 520 KB response
SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:43573
```

```bash
pnpm test extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-observe.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence:**

BEFORE FIX — CDP `Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream` + `Fetch.fulfillRequest`: 200 lines, CDP intercepts at Response stage → page receives truncated body

AFTER FIX — `body()` + `subarray()` + content-length pre-reject: 80 lines, no interception → page receives original response untouched

| Test suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| CLI oversized tests | 1 file, 4 tests passed |
| Response-body tests | 1 file, 15 tests passed |

Real browser proof (Playwright Chromium, headless, 520 KB response):

```
Tool returns bounded prefix (8000 < 520000): ✅
Page receives full original body (520000 === 520000): ✅
Page receives correct status (200): ✅
page.on('response') is passive — page delivery unaffected: ✅
```

**Observed result after the fix:** All 19 tests pass. CLI shows meaningful oversized-response notice instead of blank output. Content-length pre-reject avoids `resp.body()` entirely for known-large responses.

**What was not tested:** Extremely large responses (>500 MB) — `resp.body()` still allocates a full Buffer for non-pre-rejected responses. Chunked/unknown-length responses without content-length header still call `resp.body()` + subarray. This is a decode-only mitigation, not true streaming capture — accepted trade-off vs. the CDP page-delivery truncation bug.

## Tests and validation

- **4 CLI tests pass** covering: oversized message display, normal body output, flag validation, timeout passthrough
- **15 response-body tests pass** covering: bounded decode for small/large/chunked responses, negative control, mutation test
- **Lint clean**
- **Lines:** +39 across 3 files (source +21, tests +18)

## Risk checklist

- **Risk level:** Low — removed the risky CDP path, unified to passive observer + content-length pre-reject.
- **Mitigation:** No CDP session management. No Fetch domain manipulation. No page response interception.
- **Merge-risk explanation:** Low — CLI users now see an explicit oversized-response notice instead of blank output.
- **User-visible behavior change:** CLI `responsebody` non-JSON output shows `"(response body omitted: content-length exceeds max-bytes limit)"` for known-large responses instead of blank output.
- **Config/env/migration change?** No.
- **Security/auth/network change?** No.

## Linked context

Pattern from PR #98496 (bounded response body reads to prevent OOM). CDP approach attempted in earlier revisions of this PR, removed after ClawSweeper review identified page-delivery truncation.

target.title: fix(agents): send session_id affinity header to ChatGPT Responses backend
target.body:
Fixes #100232

### Problem
The agent-runtime OpenAI Responses transport (`createOpenAIResponsesClient` →
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders`) never sends a `session_id` header. The ChatGPT backend
(chatgpt.com/backend-api) routes requests by `session_id` — codex-cli sends it on every
request (thread id), and OpenClaw's own SSE/WS provider path (`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`)
already sets it. Without it, each HTTP request from a session can land on a different
backend machine, whose local prompt cache doesn't hold the session's prefix.

Observed on live traffic (gpt-5.5, ChatGPT OAuth): cold-write streaks and *interleaved cache
lineages* — `cached_tokens` alternating between two values (e.g. ~28k and ~57k) across
consecutive turns of one session, i.e. two machines each holding a different partial prefix.
Aggregate TRUE cache hit rate ~47-56% vs codex-cli's ~92-96% on the same account/model.

### Fix
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders()` takes an optional `sessionId`; when
`usesNativeOpenAICodexResponsesBackend(model)` and no `session_id` was set by
caller/turn headers (caller-wins preserved), it adds `session_id: <sessionId>`. Threaded
from `options?.sessionId` at the single Responses-client call site. Scoped strictly to the
native ChatGPT/Codex backend — api.openai.com and proxy endpoints are untouched.

### Measurements (12 identical prompts per leg, fresh session each, same account/hour)
| Config | TRUE hit% = cache_read/(cache_read+input) |
|---|---|
| stock | 56.0% |
| + this fix (as a dist hot-patch) | **81.8%** |
(For reference: codex-cli on the same account ~92-96%; remaining gap is its
`previous_response_id`+delta continuation, out of scope here.)

A separate controlled A/B (identical tool-call sequences, same session shape) comparing
stock vs. the combined local fix set measured **45.9% → 92.0%** TRUE hit rate — 6.5x fewer
uncached input tokens for identical work (stock session `3017333e`: 466,088 uncached input
tokens; fixed session `b97d343e`: 71,478). This isolates the session_id header's own
contribution (56.0% → 81.8%, table above) from an additional byte-stable-prefix fix tracked
separately in a follow-up PR.

Also adds a NOTE comment (no behavior change) at the WS `websocketRequestId` fallback in
`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`, which mints a fresh random id per request when
`options.sessionId` is absent — forfeiting affinity on that transport; worth a follow-up.

### Tests
4 unit tests: header present iff native backend + sessionId; absent without sessionId;
absent for `openai-responses`/api.openai.com; caller-supplied `session_id` not overwritten.
Typecheck (`run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`) clean. (Vitest currently fails to launch
on this dev box for unrelated toolchain reasons — rolldown native binding; tests were
written against the existing patterns in `openai-transport-stream.test.ts`.)

Reported-by: @Peetiegonzalez
cc: @Peetiegonzalez

## What Problem This Solves

The ChatGPT Responses backend (chatgpt.com/backend-api) routes HTTP requests by `session_id`.
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders()` never sent one, so consecutive requests from the same OpenClaw
session could land on different backend machines, each holding a different partial prompt-cache
prefix — visible as interleaved cache lineages and cold-write streaks on live traffic. codex-cli
(external reference client) and OpenClaw's own WS/SSE path already send this header; only the
HTTP Responses transport used by the `openclaw` agent runtime was missing it. See "Problem" above
for the full mechanism and code path.

## Evidence

Measured, not estimated: 12 identical prompts per leg, fresh session each, same account and same
hour, ChatGPT-OAuth gpt-5.5, `TRUE hit% = cache_read / (cache_read + input)` computed from each
call's provider `usage` fields.

- Single-variable isolation (session_id header only, all else equal): **56.0% -> 81.8%** TRUE hit
  rate (+25.8 points), cache lineage streaks disappear.
- Combined with the companion byte-stability fix (#100272), same protocol: **45.9% -> 92.0%**
  TRUE hit rate, 6.5x fewer uncached input tokens for identical 12-turn work (466,088 -> 71,478
  uncached tokens).
- Full per-call tables, regression timeline (traced to a runtime-pin config change, not a code
  regression), and cross-provider blast-radius analysis:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-session-affinity-header/pr-proof/100233-session-affinity-header/EVIDENCE.md

target.title: fix(test): unit tests fail on built checkouts and live host configs while CI stays green
target.body:
Related: #100046

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the full test suite fails deterministically on developer and maintainer machines while CI stays green, blocking local `scripts/pr` landing gates. Two host-state leaks cause it:

1. After `pnpm build`, bundled-plugin manifest discovery prefers `dist/extensions`, which by design excludes externalized official plugins (e.g. qwen, excluded via `package.json` `"!dist/extensions/qwen/**"`). Tests that rely on manifest-driven endpoint classification — the DashScope cases in `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` and `src/agents/model-compat.test.ts` — then fail in *any* built checkout, because `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/...` no longer classifies as `modelstudio-native`.
2. The `unit-fast` and `unit-fast-fake-timers` shards ran with `setupFiles: []`, so their auto-curated tests read the developer's real `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. Any config key the branch's schema doesn't know (e.g. a key written by a newer local gateway) deterministically fails config-reading tests such as `src/agents/tools/message-tool.internal-source-reply.integration.test.ts` and `src/commands/status.summary.runtime.test.ts` with `Invalid config at ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

Both classes were hit repeatedly during the landing attempts for #100046 (13 gate runs on 2026-07-04/05); #100053 fixed the discovery half for lane-invoked runs at the gate level, but plain `pnpm test` in a built checkout still failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tests should be hermetic by construction, not per-invoker env. `test/test-env.ts` (the shared isolated-home installer) now pins `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` to the repo's source `extensions/` tree alongside the existing vitest trust opt-in, so discovery matches CI (no dist) regardless of local build state; discovery unit tests keep managing that env per case (`src/plugins/bundled-dir.test.ts` deletes/sets it explicitly). The fast shards get a new minimal `test/setup.env.ts` that installs the isolated test home without the shared setup's module mocks, preserving their no-mock/no-runner speed contract. Non-goal: the load-sensitive real-timer tests (ms-budget `vi.waitFor` assertions) are a separate follow-up.

## User Impact

Maintainers and agents can run `pnpm test` in built checkouts and on machines with live OpenClaw configs and get CI-equivalent results; `scripts/pr` landing gates stop failing on these two deterministic classes. No runtime/product behavior changes — test infrastructure only.

## Evidence

- Root-cause chain for the discovery leak verified in source: `resolveBundledDirFromPackageRoot` prefers `dist/extensions` in built source checkouts (`src/plugins/bundled-dir.ts`), qwen is dist-excluded by design, and `resolveManifestProviderEndpoint` (`src/agents/provider-attribution.ts`) then loses the `modelstudio-native` endpoint class; `image.test.ts` fails with `expected 'Describe the image.' to be undefined`, and passes 29/29 with discovery pinned to source `extensions/` (verified 2026-07-05 in a built checkout).
- Config-leak failures reproduced with a live host config containing a schema-unknown key (`gateway: Unrecognized key: "terminal"`): the two unit-fast tests fail without isolation and pass with the isolated home installed.
- `bundled-dir.test.ts` unaffected: it deletes/sets `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` per case and restores the original value.
- Lane runs on the PR head via `scripts/pr review-tests` / hosted gates (see PR checks).

target.title: feat(ui): declutter the Control UI sidebar with customizable pinned nav and a More section
target.body:
Closes #100287

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sidebar had become the busiest surface in the app: three always-expanded nav groups (Control, Agent, Settings) with 13 entries, the session list, a brand header with its own collapse button, and footer utilities all competing with the chat. There was no way to choose which destinations stay visible, so every page carried the full nav tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar is restructured around a small user-customizable pinned set, modeled on how the Codex desktop app keeps a few important sections on top and hides the rest behind "More". Sessions stay first (New session, Recent, All sessions), a pinned trio follows (default: Overview, Workboard, Agents), and every other destination lives in a collapsed **More** section. Right-clicking the nav — or the "Customize sidebar" entry under More — opens a menu with per-destination pin checkmarks and a reset action; the selection persists per browser in the existing Control UI settings store (`sidebarPinnedRoutes`, `sidebarMoreExpanded`), replacing the retired per-group collapse map. Settings moved to the sidebar footer next to Docs, and the sidebar collapse toggle moved out of the brand header into the topbar as a small icon button next to the terminal toggle (hidden at drawer breakpoints where the hamburger takes over).

## User Impact

The default sidebar shows 3 nav items instead of 13, so the chat gets the visual focus. Users can pin exactly the destinations they use (right-click → check/uncheck, or More → Customize sidebar), collapse the sidebar from the topbar, and their choices survive reloads. Nothing is removed: every page stays reachable through More, Settings sits in the footer, and mobile drawer behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots are captured against the mocked-gateway e2e harness (same session fixture, dark mode, 1440×900) — see the first PR comment for the images.

- `pnpm test ui/src/app-navigation ui/src/app/settings.node ui/src/pages/overview/view.render ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view ui/src/e2e/session-management` — remote Testbox run (IDs in PR comment).

target.title: fix(mcp): suppress unhandled rejection from async gateway event handler
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `onEvent` callback in `OpenClawChannelBridge` calls `void this.handleGatewayEvent(event)` without observing the returned promise. Since `handleGatewayEvent` is async and can reject, this creates an unhandled promise rejection that crashes the MCP gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Contain the async handler rejection and emit a low-noise diagnostic, matching the existing notification-failure observability pattern in the same bridge (`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:399`). Failed session or approval events are therefore visible to operators instead of disappearing silently.

## User Impact

Prevents the gateway from crashing when an MCP channel bridge event handler throws, while keeping failures observable.

## Evidence

### Behavior

The `onEvent` callback now delegates to `dispatchGatewayEvent`, which awaits `handleGatewayEvent` inside a `try/catch`. On rejection it writes exactly one stderr record (`openclaw mcp: gateway event <type> failed`), with the full error shown only when `--verbose` is on.

### Source

`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:150`
```ts
onEvent: (event) => {
  void this.dispatchGatewayEvent(event);
},
```

`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:524`
```ts
private async dispatchGatewayEvent(event: EventFrame): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await this.handleGatewayEvent(event);
  } catch (error) {
    // Always surface a single low-noise record so swallowed gateway event
    // failures remain observable; the spammy error detail stays behind --verbose.
    process.stderr.write(`openclaw mcp: gateway event ${event.event} failed\n`);
    if (this.verbose) {
      process.stderr.write(
        `openclaw mcp: gateway event ${event.event} error: ${String(error)}\n`,
      );
    }
  }
}
```

### Unit test output

```
$ pnpm test -- src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts (18 tests) 154ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  1.12s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.50s
```

### Real runtime proof

I ran a real OpenClaw MCP bridge against the local gateway (`ws://127.0.0.1:18789`) and forced `handleGatewayEvent` to reject for `session.message` events. The bridge stayed alive and emitted the expected diagnostic on stderr:

```
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message failed
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message error: Error: injected proof rejection
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message failed
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message error: Error: injected proof rejection
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message failed
openclaw mcp: gateway event session.message error: Error: injected proof rejection
```

The injection was removed before committing; the committed code only logs real failures.

### Regression coverage

- `a rejected gateway event still emits exactly one diagnostic record with verbose off`
- `a rejected gateway event includes error detail with verbose on`

Both tests force `handleGatewayEvent` to reject, call `dispatchGatewayEvent`, and assert the exact stderr output shape while confirming the error detail is redacted unless verbose is enabled.

target.title: fix(proxy): apply enhanced NO_PROXY matching to global undici dispatcher (fixes #95998)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95998.

When `HTTPS_PROXY` is set, the global EnvHttpProxyAgent routes ALL requests through the proxy — including internal plugin requests that should bypass via `NO_PROXY`. The built-in undici NO_PROXY matcher does not support leading-dot subdomain patterns, CIDR notation, or octet wildcards.

OpenClaw already has `matchesNoProxy()` that handles these — but it was only used by provider helpers, not the global dispatcher.

## Changes Made

1. **NO_PROXY-aware proxy dispatcher** — Wraps every EnvHttpProxyAgent with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before dispatching to the direct bypass agent.

2. **Lifecycle synchronization (P1 fix)** — Promise-style `close()`/`destroy()` now await both the bypass agent AND the proxy dispatcher before settling. `destroy(err)` arguments are forwarded correctly.

3. **no_proxy precedence (P1 fix)** — Empty lowercase `no_proxy` now correctly shadows uppercase `NO_PROXY`, matching undici EnvHttpProxyAgent semantics.

## Network Boundary Change — Scope and Rationale

This PR extends OpenClaw existing `matchesNoProxy()` (already used by provider helpers) to the global undici dispatcher. This means NO_PROXY patterns that undici built-in matcher cannot handle (CIDR, octet-wildcard) will now correctly bypass the proxy at the process level.

- **Scope**: Only affects the NO_PROXY matching path. The EnvHttpProxyAgent is still used for all non-bypassed requests. Bypass agent inherits the same timeout/connect policy.
- **Risk**: `matchesNoProxy()` is already proven in production via provider helpers. This PR applies the same logic to the global dispatcher.
- **Upgrade**: Existing deployments with basic domain NO_PROXY patterns are unaffected. Deployments using CIDR or octet-wildcard entries will see those patterns start working (previously broken).
- **Lifecycle safety**: close/destroy synchronizes both dispatchers. Promise-style and callback-style both work correctly.

## Evidence

**Enhanced matcher proof (18/18 tests passed):**
```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx _matcher_proof.mjs

=== Enhanced NO_PROXY Matcher Proof ===
(Core of PR #97713 — the dispatcher wrapper uses matchesNoProxy())

  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Subdomain: .myqcloud.com, COS bucket: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, deep nested: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, matching: true
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, matching (CGNAT): true
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, matching (link-local): true
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, non-matching: false
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, matching: true
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, non-matching: false
  ✅ Precedence: no_proxy shadows NO_PROXY: true
  ✅ Precedence: empty no_proxy blocks uppercase: false
  ✅ Precedence: only NO_PROXY falls back: true

CIDR/Octet-wildcard tests: 8/8 passed
(Undici v8.5.0 built-in NO_PROXY matcher does NOT support CIDR or octet-wildcard patterns)
Total: 18/18 passed (0 failed)
```

**Unit tests (90/90 passed):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/proxy-env.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted: Yes
- Manually reviewed and verified

## False Positive Risk Mitigation

The enhanced NO_PROXY matcher (`matchesNoProxy()`) is already used by provider helpers in production — this PR extends the same proven logic to the global dispatcher. The false positive risk is inherently limited because:

1. **Pattern-gated**: The enhanced matcher only triggers when the NO_PROXY value actually contains CIDR, octet-wildcard, or leading-dot patterns. For plain domain matching, the behavior is identical to undici built-in.
2. **Already deployed**: Provider helpers (SSRF guard, per-request routing) have used `matchesNoProxy()` in production without incident.
3. **Conservative**: The bypass agent inherits the same timeout and connect policy as the EnvHttpProxyAgent, so bypassed requests behave identically to proxied ones — just without the proxy hop.
4. **Auditable**: The `matchesNoProxy()` logic is contained in a single function (`src/infra/net/proxy-env.ts`) and is covered by 55 unit tests.

Maintainers should explicitly accept the broader proxy-bypass boundary before merge (see Network Boundary section above).


## Proof of Global Dispatcher Routing

The PR changes the global undici dispatcher by wrapping it with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before routing. Each dispatched request follows this flow:

1. `dispatch()` is called on the Proxy wrapper
2. If `hasEnvHttpProxyAgentConfigured() && matchesNoProxy(origin)` → route through **bypass Agent** (direct, no proxy)
3. Otherwise → route through **EnvHttpProxyAgent** (through proxy)

This logic is verified by:

- **35 dispatcher tests** — `undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts` covers proxy wrapper creation, dispatch routing, lifecycle sync, and bypass agent behavior
- **55 proxy-env tests** — `proxy-env.test.ts` covers all `matchesNoProxy()` patterns (CIDR, octet-wildcard, subdomain, precedence)
- **18 matcher scenarios** — verified individually with terminal output above

The 90 unit tests run against the actual undici runtime and confirm the wrapper correctly:
- Forwards matching requests to the bypass agent
- Forwards non-matching requests to the EnvHttpProxyAgent
- Synchronizes close/destroy lifecycle
- Preserves `no_proxy` precedence


## Live Proxy Proof

A local HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:18999 was configured as HTTPS_PROXY. The NO_PROXY-aware dispatcher was set as the global undici dispatcher, then fetch() requests were made under different NO_PROXY settings. The proxy logged every CONNECT attempt.

```
1. Without NO_PROXY:
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

2. NO_PROXY=example.com (matching):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://example.com)  ← intercepted

3. NO_PROXY=other.com (non-matching):
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

4. NO_PROXY=100.64.0.0/10 (CIDR — undici lacks this):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://100.100.0.1)  ← CIDR works
```

target.title: feat(commands): move /new to the top of native command menu
target.body:
Move the /new command (start a new session) to be the first entry in the built-in native command registry, making it appear first in Telegram/Discord bot command menus.

/new is by far the most frequently used command in daily workflows. Placing it first reduces friction for users who reach for it constantly, similar to how Hermes prioritizes it.

Before: help, commands, tools, ..., reset, new, compact, ...
After:  new, help, commands, tools, ..., reset, compact, ...

target.title: fix(agents): retry same profile before timeout auth rotation
target.body:
## Summary

This PR keeps ordinary assistant-stage timeouts from immediately spending an auth-profile rotation. A first ordinary timeout now gets one bounded retry on the same model/profile; if the retry budget is exhausted, the existing auth-profile rotation path still runs.

The change deliberately does **not** weaken real failover for rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures. Those reasons continue through the existing profile rotation / escalation path rather than being hidden by the timeout retry.

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary assistant-stage timeout is not necessarily evidence that the current auth profile is bad. Rotating the auth profile on the first ordinary timeout can spend a scarce profile/fallback lane too early and make transient timeout handling look like an auth-profile failure.

This patch keeps the first ordinary timeout local to the same model/profile retry budget while preserving the existing fast-failover behavior for real auth/rate-limit/quota/billing-style failures.

## Why this is not covered by adjacent timeout fixes

Related timeout/failover work already exists, but it addresses adjacent seams rather than this one:

- #80449 made idle watchdog timeouts participate in profile/model failover.
- #87538 made timeout cooldowns model-scoped, so one model timeout does not block unrelated fallback models on the same profile.
- #1576 classifies provider `Request was aborted` errors as timeout-like for fallback.
- #95650 is about compaction retry behavior with backup auth profiles.
- #87122 is about provider overload cooldown semantics.

Current `origin/main` still only has the idle-timeout-specific same-model retry gate (`same_model_idle_timeout`). It does not have an ordinary request-timeout same-profile retry gate before `advanceAuthProfile()`.

## Behavior addressed

Before this patch, an ordinary assistant-stage timeout could be classified as `rotate_profile` and call `advanceAuthProfile()` on the first timeout, marking the current profile as a timeout failure.

After this patch:

- ordinary assistant-stage timeout: retry the same model/profile once first;
- repeated ordinary timeout after the retry budget is exhausted: use the existing auth-profile rotation path;
- rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures: keep existing fast failover behavior;
- compaction/tool-execution timeouts: remain excluded from this assistant-stage retry gate;
- configured fallback is intentionally not a bypass for the first ordinary timeout; the retry budget is one, so fallback/rotation remains available on the next timeout.

## Implementation notes

- Generalizes the previous idle-only retry state from `same_model_idle_timeout` to `same_model_timeout`.
- Keeps the retry budget bounded at one same-profile retry.
- Adds an ordinary-timeout guard so unrelated failure reasons are not masked by a timeout flag.
- Extracts `shouldAllowSameModelTimeoutRetry` so the run-loop gate is directly tested for ordinary timeout, compaction/tool-execution exclusion, restart support, and retry budget.
- Leaves the existing rate-limit short-window retry and overload/profile-rotation behavior intact.

## Session-state blocker addressed in this update

After the proof review, ClawSweeper moved the remaining blocker from proof to `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: the timeout retry path must not expand a known transcript replay hazard where an aborted empty assistant leaf can remain before the trailing-user repair path.

This head includes the same transcript-safe repair from sibling PR #95766:

- drops an empty aborted assistant leaf before checking/repairing the trailing-user invariant;
- covers the helper behavior in `attempt.prompt-helpers.test.ts`;
- preserves the timeout retry behavior from this PR while avoiding an additional session-state replay risk.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Runtime proof: local OpenAI-compatible timeout service

I re-ran this PR through the actual embedded runtime, not only the helper. The proof uses:

- current PR head: `3414cee48409b1b4fe3b765e71b6ff493185f322`
- `openclaw agent --local` from this PR checkout
- a temporary isolated user home, OpenClaw config, state directory, and workspace
- a local OpenAI-compatible Responses service with its endpoint/port redacted
- synthetic model names: `timeout-primary` and `fallback-ok`
- no live gateway, no production state, no external provider call, and no real credentials

The local service intentionally holds the first two `timeout-primary` Responses requests past the configured 1 second provider timeout, then returns a valid streamed Responses success for `fallback-ok`.

Observed runtime request order:

```text
POST /v1/responses request #1 model=timeout-primary  -> provider timeout
POST /v1/responses request #2 model=timeout-primary  -> same model/profile retry before fallback
POST /v1/responses request #3 model=fallback-ok      -> streamed success
```

Observed final visible payload:

```text

```

Redacted runtime log excerpts:

```text

[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=fallback_model reason=timeout from=openai/timeout-primary profile=- rawError=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/timeout-primary candidate=openai/timeout-primary reason=timeout next=openai/fallback-ok detail=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
```

target.title: fix(models): resolve provider-qualified aliases
target.body:
Closes #75163

Reworks the useful direction from #75198 on current `main`, with provider-scoped duplicate handling and contributor credit preserved.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users switching an existing Control UI or TUI session to a provider-qualified display alias such as `lmstudio-moe/MoE` would persist `MoE` as the model id. Local providers then rejected the next turn because the display alias was not their canonical model identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared model resolver now indexes aliases by provider as well as by bare display name, so `provider/Alias` resolves without colliding when two providers use the same alias. Chat-command model selection now delegates to that same resolver instead of maintaining a second parser.

## User Impact

Mid-session model switches from Control UI, TUI, and model commands now persist the canonical provider/model reference. Existing bare-alias behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 121 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 228 tests passed across the routed Gateway shards.

target.title: feat(ui): scroll truncated sidebar session names on hover
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long session titles in the Control UI sidebar's recent-sessions list get clipped with an ellipsis, and there is no way to read the hidden tail without opening the session or waiting for the native tooltip. Titles like "Fix stale iMessage group-allowlist warning copy" become indistinguishable once several sessions share a prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hovering a session row now animates the truncated label so the clipped tail scrolls into view (marquee-style), and the label snaps back quickly when the pointer leaves. The animation transitions `text-indent` rather than transforming an inner wrapper because `text-overflow` renders no ellipsis for atomic inline children — the wrapper approach would have lost the resting "…". Scroll duration is proportional to the hidden distance (80px/s, 300ms minimum) so short and long titles both stay readable, labels that fit are left untouched, and `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps the static ellipsis. The helper (`ui/src/lib/hover-marquee.ts`) plus generic `.hover-marquee` CSS are reusable for other truncated labels (e.g. the sessions table or session picker) as follow-ups; this PR wires only the requested sidebar surface.

## User Impact

Hovering a truncated session name in the sidebar scrolls the full title into view; moving the mouse away restores the normal ellipsized label. No behavior change for labels that fit, keyboard users, or reduced-motion users.

target.title: fix: prevent Anthropic thinking-signature replay causing permanent session bricks (#94228)
target.body:
## Summary

This PR implements a create-side prevention fix for Issue #94228, where Anthropic thinking-signature replay causes permanent session bricks.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The current implementation re-emits ALL historical thinking blocks with their original signatures during replay, violating Anthropic's contract that "thinking blocks from already-closed turns may be omitted". When signatures become stale (due to model version drift, config changes, or internal state corruption), this causes HTTP 400 errors and permanent session bricks (~11 occurrences/24h per host).

**Impact**: Users experience permanent session bricks requiring manual restart when thinking signatures no longer match the replay context.

## Why This Change Was Made

After analyzing 9 different PR approaches (#94493, #94649, #97019, etc.), I identified a gap in the existing sanitization pipeline:

- Current code handles compaction-stale signatures (timestamp-based)
- Current code handles blank/missing signatures
- **Missing**: Present-but-invalid signatures from other sources (model drift, config changes, corruption)

This fix fills that gap by unconditionally stripping ALL non-latest thinking signatures, providing defense-in-depth alongside recovery-side approaches like PR #94649.

## User Impact

**Before**: Sessions could brick permanently when stale thinking signatures were replayed, causing HTTP 400 errors on every subsequent request.

**After**: Non-latest thinking signatures are proactively stripped before replay, preventing signature mismatch errors while preserving latest-turn signatures for provider compatibility.

**Performance**: Minimal impact - returns original array reference when no changes needed (reference equality optimization).

## Evidence

### Code Changes
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.ts`: Added `stripAllNonLatestThinkingSignatures()` (+62 lines)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts`: Integrated into `sanitizeSessionHistory` pipeline (+16 lines)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.test.ts`: Comprehensive test coverage (+152 lines)

### Test Coverage
6 test cases covering:
1. Reference equality when no non-latest turns exist
2. Strips ALL signature types (valid, blank, missing, opaque) from non-latest turns
3. Preserves all signatures with single turn + preserveLatestAssistant: false
4. Can strip from "latest" turn when flag disabled
5. Handles multiple turns correctly
6. Generates placeholder text for thinking-only turns

### Design Principles
- **Minimal scope**: ~60 lines core logic, following PR #94649 example
- **Leverages existing helpers**: Uses `stripThinkingSignaturesFromMessage`
- **Defensive design**: Latest-turn exemption protects provider expectations
- **Performance optimized**: Returns original array when unchanged
- **Comprehensive testing**: 6 cases covering edge cases

### Integration Point
Inserted into `sanitizeSessionHistory` pipeline between:
1. `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay` (compaction-specific)
2. **NEW** `stripAllNonLatestThinkingSignatures` (universal prevention)
3. `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` (final safety net)

## Relationship to Other Fixes

This create-side prevention complements PR #94649 recovery-side approach:

| Layer | Mechanism | Timing | This PR | PR #94649 |
|-------|-----------|--------|---------|-----------|
| Prevention | Create-side sanitization | Before request sent | ✅ Strips non-latest signatures | ❌ |
| Recovery | Terminal-result carrier | After error detected | ❌ | ✅ Retries without thinking |
| Repair | Reactive history repair | After provider confirms rejection | ❌ | ✅ `repairRejectedThinkingReplayInSessionManager` |

Three layers working together provide robust protection against thinking-signature bricks.

## Testing Notes

Due to network firewall blocking external AI APIs (`api.anthropic.com` redirected to block page), I could not perform live reproduction of the thinking-signature brick scenario. Implementation based on thorough source code analysis across 9 different PR approaches.

Tests can be validated via CI or by maintainers with direct API access.

## Coordination Questions

- Is this PR waiting on any other PR to merge first?
- Are maintainers planning coordinated fix under #94228, or preferring incremental patches?
- Should contributors focus on one approach (recovery vs prevention) to avoid conflicts?

Happy to help however makes sense - whether providing additional repro evidence (once network access resolved), testing existing PRs, or diving into narrower follow-up issues!

---

**Fixes**: #94228
**Related**: #94649, #94493, #97019, #94234, #98441, #98831

target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled rejection from async abort callback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the agent session extension abort callback called `session.abort()` asynchronously and ignored the returned promise. If `session.abort()` ever rejects (for example due to a future regression in run shutdown or an extension-provided abort path that delegates here), the rejection would become an unhandled rejection and could crash the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a `.catch()` handler to the fire-and-forget `this.abort()` call in the extension abort callback. The handler writes a stderr diagnostic (`agent-session: extension abort failed: ...`) so the failure is observable without propagating as an unhandled rejection. This is defense-in-depth: current `Agent.waitForIdle()` normally resolves the active run promise, so the rejecting path is not reproducible under normal runtime conditions, but the callback boundary is now guarded against future regressions.

## User Impact

Extension abort handling is more resilient; a rare or future abort failure is logged to stderr instead of surfacing as an unhandled rejection that could terminate the session or process.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/agent-session-void-abort-catch`

**Proof command**:
```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts
```

**Proof output**:
```
=== Proof: agent session extension abort catch ===

Calling extension runtime abort callback with a rejecting session.abort()...

agent-session: extension abort failed: Error: simulated abort rejection

PASS: rejecting abort is caught and logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
```

The proof creates a real `AgentSession`, stubs its `abort()` to reject, invokes the bound extension runtime `abortFn`, and captures stderr to confirm the diagnostic is written.

**Regression test**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The regression test "logs a diagnostic when the extension abort fallback rejects" exercises the same synthetic rejecting-abort path and asserts the stderr diagnostic.

target.title: feat(scripts): serialize pr prepare gates and add remote Testbox test gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` landing gates run the full `pnpm test` (88 vitest shards) locally in the `.worktrees/<pr>` checkout and require it green before `prepare-push`/`merge-run`. On a maintainer Mac that also runs VMs and other agent sessions this is effectively un-passable: shards stall >120s under load and the `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` no-output watchdog SIGTERMs them, and a concurrent `scripts/pr` gate run's children die on the shared heavy-check lock's 10-minute timeout while its unlocked `pnpm build` piles more load onto the holder's shards. Observed repeatedly landing PRs #99935/#100026 on 2026-07-04/05: zero real test failures, only watchdog kills and lock contention with a concurrent run for `.worktrees/pr-100046`. Root `AGENTS.md` validation policy already says full suites belong on Crabbox/Testbox, not the Mac.

Fixes #100226.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`OPENCLAW_PR_GATES_REMOTE=testbox`** (opt-in; local stays the default): `prepare_gates` and the lease-retry gates run the same full-suite `pnpm test` on a Blacksmith Testbox through `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox ...` — the exact delegation shape `pnpm check:changed` already uses (same workflow `.github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml`, job `check`). The worktree's own wrapper copy is used deliberately so the crabbox sync ships the prep tree, not the primary checkout. The `tbx_` lease id and Actions run URL from the crabbox `--timing-json` report (single-line JSON on stderr; verified against `../crabbox` `internal/cli/timing.go` and `internal/providers/blacksmith/backend.go`) are recorded in `.local/gates.env` as `REMOTE_GATES_PROVIDER` / `REMOTE_GATES_LEASE_ID` / `REMOTE_GATES_RUN_URL` with `GATES_MODE=remote_testbox`, and surface in `.local/prep.md` at `prepare-push`. `pnpm build`/`pnpm check` stay local. Unsupported values fail fast, and combining with `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1` (hosted exact-head evidence) is rejected as ambiguous.
- **Whole-block gate serialization**: `scripts/pr-gates-lock.mjs` holds the existing shared heavy-check lock (`toolName: "pr-gates"`, 2h default wait instead of the 10-minute per-command default) for the entire local gate block; gate stages inherit the same `OPENCLAW_TEST_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_HELD`/`OPENCLAW_TSGO_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_HELD`/`OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_LOCK` child contract `check:changed` already uses, so they don't re-acquire. Concurrent gate runs across `.worktrees` now queue as whole units before their first command instead of dying mid-test. The holder releases on SIGTERM, on gate-shell death (ppid watch), and stays covered by the lock runtime's owner-pid reclaim; in remote mode the lock is released before the remote test so the Mac stays usable.
- **Lease-retry stamp integrity** (autoreview finding, fixed): when a lease retry rebases the prep head and reruns gates, the retry path now rewrites `.local/gates.env` for the new head through the shared `write_gates_env_stamp` writer, and `prepare_push` re-sources it, so `prep.md`/`prep.env` never attribute stale gate evidence (mode, heads, or Testbox lease) to the pushed commit.

## User Impact

Maintainer tooling only (no product/runtime surface). `scripts/pr prepare-gates`/`prepare-run` become passable on loaded hosts via a sanctioned remote full-test gate with an auditable Testbox stamp, and concurrent landings no longer kill each other's gates. Default behavior on an idle host is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Behavior tests: `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (17 tests) — mode resolution + hosted-mode conflict, exact wrapper argv, stamp extraction (last successful report wins; failure-only logs rejected), lease-retry stamp refresh (remote + local), lock helper acquire/queue/SIGTERM-release/parent-death-release/timeout-failure, and the bash acquire/release env contract. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` → 17 passed; sibling `pr-wrappers` + `verify-pr-hosted-gates` suites → 6 passed.
- Remote Testbox `check:changed` over this diff (lanes docs+tooling incl. `lint scripts`): exit 0, lease `tbx_01kwrne1rn5q9212yahvphf5k9`, 1m56s.
- Live busy-Mac verification (load average ~20, real open PR worktree `.worktrees/pr-100046`, `OPENCLAW_PR_GATES_REMOTE=testbox`): `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` passed locally while `owner.json` showed the gate lock held as `"tool": "pr-gates"`, the lock released before delegation, and the full suite ran on Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kwrp4esmb266qeh0nxfvjns4` — 89 shards in 776s, 3 shards genuinely red on that PR's stale prep tree (`unit-fast`, `extension-diffs`, `extension-acpx`), so the gate **failed closed**: exit 1, failure digest + rerun commands printed, crabbox failure bundle captured, and no `.local/gates.env` stamp written.
- Success-path stamp on live data: the parser extracts `tbx_01kwrne1rn5q9212yahvphf5k9` from the real successful crabbox timing report and extracts nothing from the real failed gate log; the stamp write itself is covered by the lease-retry tests. The ambient-env conflict guard also fired live (this session exports `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1`), refusing the remote mode until the harness cleared it.
- Not run: a green end-to-end remote gate (both candidate PR trees were red or mid-landing by another session) and a full local 88-shard default-mode run on a quiet host — the local test invocation is byte-identical to `main` apart from the lock wrap, which the live build/check run and the lock tests cover.

Autoreview (codex/gpt-5.5): first pass found the lease-retry stale-stamp issue (fixed above); rerun clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

target.title: fix(codex): use UTF-16-safe truncation for approval display paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The codex app-server approval and elicitation bridges truncate user-provided text (command previews, approval titles, display parameter values) using raw `String.prototype.slice`. When the truncation boundary falls between the high and low surrogate of a supplementary-plane character (emoji, CJK extension, etc.), the output contains a lone surrogate — corrupted UTF-16.

This is the same class of bug fixed in #99566 for `exec-approval-command-display.ts`. The shared `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` helpers (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`) already back off from split surrogate pairs at the boundary; they are used by 20+ other extensions but were not yet adopted in these three codex bridge files.

Relates to gap finding: `codex-utf16-safe-truncation` (`utf16-boundary`, evidence level A)
Location: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.ts:1498`

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `String.prototype.slice` with `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` in all 6 call sites across 3 source files:

| File | Function | Cap | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `truncate()` | 48–180 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `previewSource()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `appendPreviewPart()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `sanitizeDisplayText()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `truncateDisplayText()` | 120 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `plugin-approval-roundtrip.ts` | `truncateForGateway()` | 80, 256 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |

The SDK helpers are dependency-free, already exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, and already in use within the same extension (`node-cli-sessions.ts:698`). Cap sizes, truncation markers, and redaction order are unchanged.

## User Impact

Affects codex app-server users whose command previews or approval display text contain emoji or other astral-plane characters near the truncation boundary. Before this fix, a dangling high surrogate could appear in approval prompts; after, the emoji is dropped as a unit and the preceding character is preserved.

## Evidence

### 1. Rebased onto upstream/main (2026-07-05)

Branch rebased onto `upstream/main` (`e6ec74c254`) to pick up latest doc snapshots. No merge conflicts. Commits cleanly apply.

### 2. Real Codex app-server spawn + helper verification

Real `codex` CLI v0.142.5 spawned as `codex app-server --listen stdio://`. The process accepts JSON-RPC `initialize` requests and responds with protocol handshake — confirming the binary is functional for app-server transport.

Against the **same built dist** used by the running gateway, the imported `sliceUtf16Safe` / `truncateUtf16Safe` helpers from `packages/normalization-core/dist/utf16-slice.mjs` are exercised with surrogate-pair inputs matching all three PR-affected truncation boundaries:

```

    Input: aaa...aaa😀tail (182 UTF-16)
    Raw  slice(0,177) -> 177u, lone=true (BUG!)
    Safe slice(0,177) -> 176u, lone=false

[2] truncateUtf16Safe (approval-bridge truncate pattern)
    Raw  trunc(177)  -> 177u, lone=true (BUG!)
    Safe trunc(177)  -> 176u, lone=false

[3] Elicitation truncateDisplayText pattern (117 char boundary)
    Input 122u, trunc(117) -> 116u, lone=false

[4] Gateway truncateForGateway pattern
    Input 202u, trunc(197) -> 196u, lone=false

[5] Multiple emoji types at slice boundaries
    grin: PASS
    rocket: PASS
    tada: PASS
    skull: PASS
    family: PASS

[6] Real Codex app-server spawn & JSON-RPC exchange

    Init response: OK

Fix verified:       YES (UTF-16-safe helpers avoid lone surrogates)
```

target.title: feat(android): syntax-highlighted code blocks in chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fenced code blocks in Android chat render as flat monospace text, making code-heavy assistant replies hard to scan.

Part of #100195

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a minimal in-repo tokenizer (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatCodeHighlight.kt`) for kotlin/swift/typescript/javascript/python/bash/json with keyword/string/comment/number classes. An external highlighting library was evaluated and rejected: ~10 months without releases/commits, single maintainer, and no JSON support, versus ~300 lines of owned, testable code with no license-screen overhead. Token colors are new `MobileColors` code-palette slots (light+dark, ≥4.5:1 contrast against the code background). Streaming stays cheap: still-open fences render plain while a message streams (gated on CommonMark `closingFenceLength` + stream state), results are memoized per block content, and blocks over 200 lines or 20k chars fall back to plain rendering.

## User Impact

Assistant code blocks in chat get readable, theme-aware syntax coloring in light and dark mode. Unknown languages, streaming partial blocks, and very large blocks keep today's plain rendering. No config or behavior surface changes.

## Evidence

- `apps/android`: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests '*ChatMarkdown*' --tests '*AndroidLicenseNotices*'` — 20 tests, 0 failures (same green on `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest`)
- New tests in `ChatMarkdownTest.kt`: known-language tokens, theme span colors, unknown-language plain fallback, open-fence detection, line/char bounds incl. exact 200-line boundary, escaped quotes, bash comment boundaries, nested block comments, multiline template literals/shell strings
- Codex autoreview: 6 iterative rounds during development; 8 accepted findings fixed, each with a regression test; final run clean ("patch is correct", 0.88)

Known gap: unit-test proof only; no emulator screenshot pass of the rendered palette yet.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(qqbot): channel status keeps reporting connected after the gateway websocket dies
target.body:
**Prompt request:** Make the QQBot channel report `connected: false` (with the close reason for permanent stops) whenever its gateway websocket closes, permanently stops, or exhausts reconnect attempts, while preserving the existing reconnect and lifecycle behavior.

**Proof target:** Show that after a fatal close the channel status flips to `connected: false` with the reason in `lastError`, and that READY and RESUMED still restore `connected: true`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators checking `openclaw channels status` (or any consumer of the gateway `channels.status` method) would see a QQBot account reported as `connected: true` even though the gateway websocket was down, including permanently dead states such as a banned or offline bot (close code 4915 = banned, 4914 = offline/sandbox-only) and exhausted reconnect attempts. Every real disconnect now gives readiness and health monitoring the expected `connected: false` failure signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QQBot channel only ever wrote `connected: true` (on READY and RESUMED); no close path updated the status. This change adds an `onDisconnected({ reason, fatal })` callback through the QQBot gateway boundary. It does not fire for an intentional stop, and delayed close events from superseded sockets are ignored both while replacement is pending and after it is live. All real closes write raw `connected: false`; fatal closes also record the terminal reason in `lastError`. READY and RESUMED restore `connected: true` and clear stale fatal errors. Server-requested reconnect and invalid-session opcodes publish one recoverable disconnect before retiring the socket; the delayed close is deduplicated. QQBot's fatal flag still suppresses its immediate reconnect policy, the shared monitor remains separately rate-limited, and `running` remains owned by the gateway lifecycle store.

## User Impact

Operators now see truthful QQBot connection state: `connected: false` during reconnect backoff and after a fatal close, with the reason (`banned`, `offline/sandbox-only`, `reconnect attempts exhausted`) surfaced as `lastError`. Readiness no longer reports a fatally disconnected account as healthy, and the shared health monitor can apply its bounded recovery policy.

## Evidence

Current head: `5ac9f1933eda7ddb175da152c78ee4043b7338e1`.

Real behavior proof: redacted `openclaw channels status` terminal output from a real gateway run. A full OpenClaw gateway (production channel manager, QQBot plugin, `channels.status` RPC, real CLI) runs from this branch in an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with placeholder credentials; a local mock WebSocket server stands in for the QQ platform gateway and speaks the documented protocol frames (HELLO -> IDENTIFY -> READY -> RESUME -> RESUMED -> close codes), and the two QQ HTTP edge modules (token endpoint, REST gateway discovery) are stubbed at module load. Everything else, including the disconnect and status reporting path under review, is unmodified production code. Timeline: connect -> READY, transient close 4000 -> reconnect -> RESUMED, then fatal close 4914 with the mock platform refusing every subsequent session.

Before (base commit `bfffa950d7`), the status stays stale after the fatal close: the bot is permanently offline yet the channel still claims a live connection:

```text
--- channels status (after READY) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, connected, token:config
--- channels status (after transient close + RESUMED) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, connected, token:config
--- channels status (after fatal close 4914, mock platform refusing sessions) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, connected, token:config
```

After (this change), the same timeline reports the truth: RESUMED restores `connected`, and the fatal close surfaces disconnected state plus the close reason:

```text
--- channels status (after READY) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, connected, token:config
--- channels status (after transient close + RESUMED) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, connected, token:config
--- channels status (after fatal close 4914, mock platform refusing sessions) ---
- QQ Bot default: enabled, configured, running, disconnected, token:config, health:disconnected, error:offline/sandbox-only
```

Gateway log lines from the same after-run show the new disconnect notifications on the production path (`[qqbot:default] Gateway disconnected: close code 4000`, `[qqbot:default] Gateway disconnected: offline/sandbox-only`). Both transient and fatal transport failures remain visible to raw health/readiness evaluation; QQBot itself only schedules immediate reconnects for recoverable failures.

Failing-first unit tests (fail on the base commit, where no disconnect signal exists; pass with this change):

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.test.ts`: fatal close 4915 reports `{ reason: "banned", fatal: true }`; a transient close reports non-fatal; reconnect exhaustion reports `{ reason: "reconnect attempts exhausted", fatal: true }`; an intentional abort reports nothing; stale closes from superseded sockets are ignored; server-requested reconnect and invalid-session opcodes each publish exactly one recoverable disconnect.
- `extensions/qqbot/src/channel.gateway-status.test.ts`: transient and fatal raw status both flip to `connected: false`; fatal state records `lastError`; READY and RESUMED restore `connected: true` and clear the error.

Maintainer proof on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwrv0h5tzbcq6wwhezn9xc64`: full QQBot suite 74 files / 663 tests green; final-head focused status/connection proof 2 files / 10 tests green; path-scoped `pnpm check:changed` for all seven PR files green. Fresh branch autoreview on head `5ac9f1933eda7ddb175da152c78ee4043b7338e1`: no actionable findings. The generated Swift protocol drift that failed the earlier exact-head run was fixed independently on `main` by `1403c64799`, so that redundant repair was dropped during the final rebase.

Known limitation: the capture substitutes a local mock server for the live QQ platform edge (no live QQ credentials are used); close-code interpretation itself is the existing `ReconnectState.handleClose` mapping and is unchanged by this PR.

target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.
