target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: fresh clone of `pull/99954/head` (`82bc62ed46`) inside a stock `node:22-bookworm` container: `git fetch --depth 1 origin pull/99954/head && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: plain Docker container (crabbox delegated providers unavailable on this host: `blacksmith` and `sbx` binaries not installed, no AWS credentials — stated per proof policy rather than skipped silently)
- Result: **34/34 tests passed, 6/6 files** on the fresh clone

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.

target.title: fix(agents): report plugin approval request rejections
target.body:
## Summary

- Distinguish gateway request rejections from transport/unavailable failures in the plugin approval before_tool_call path.
- Surface `INVALID_REQUEST` details to the agent as `Plugin approval request rejected: ...` instead of the misleading gateway-unavailable fallback.
- Add regression coverage for both embedded-mode and full before_tool_call approval handling while preserving the transport-error fallback.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #100212.

A reachable gateway can reject `plugin.approval.request` payloads, for example when an approval title exceeds the schema's 80-character cap. Before this change, the catch block reported every non-abort request failure as `Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)`, which points operators and agents at the wrong system even when the gateway actively returned `INVALID_REQUEST`.

## Changes

- Added a small formatter for plugin approval gateway failures.
- When the caught error is `GatewayClientRequestError` with `gatewayCode === "INVALID_REQUEST"`, the returned tool-block reason now includes the sanitized request rejection message.
- Other errors still use the existing `Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)` reason.
- Added regression tests for request rejection handling in embedded and full before_tool_call approval flows.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/mcp/plugin-tools-serve.test.ts`
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Diff secret scan over `git diff HEAD~1..HEAD`

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin approval request validation failures are no longer misreported as gateway outages. Agents and operators now see that the approval request was rejected, plus the relevant validation message, so they can fix the plugin-provided approval payload instead of debugging a healthy gateway or target app.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` passed: 14 embedded-mode tests and 59 before_tool_call e2e tests.

target.title: Gateway: allow extension origins in browser allowlist
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` (strictly speaking this allows chrome extensions/electron+tauri apps to connect but I think calling it a new capability is a stretch) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: `N/A` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: local Bun + Vitest - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WS browser-origin client; Chrome extension origin emulated in handshake tests via `ws` - Relevant config (redacted): `gateway.auth.mode="token"`, `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]` ### Steps 1. Configure the Gateway with token auth and `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]`. 2. Open a WS connection that sends `Origin: chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop` and a valid `connect` request. 3. Observe the handshake result. ### Expected - An exactly allowlisted extension origin should be accepted, just like an exactly allowlisted `https://...` origin. ### Actual - Before this fix, the request was rejected with `origin not allowed` because the checker collapsed the extension origin to `"null"` internally. - After this fix, the handshake succeeds and returns `hello-ok`. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: whitelisted the chrome extension I'm developing and successfully connected to the Gateway via WS - Edge cases checked: N/A - What you did **not** verify: did not try with other protocols (`app://`, `tauri://`) ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` - If yes, exact upgrade steps: `N/A` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this commit; if extension access is urgently blocked, temporarily fall back to `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["*"]` until the regression is understood. - Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/origin-check.ts`; optionally restore prior `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` values in config. - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: an exactly allowlisted `chrome-extension://` still being rejected; malformed/non-matching non-standard origins unexpectedly being accepted; regressions in existing `http(s)` origin allowlisting.

target.title: fix(ios): defer QR pairing after scanner dismissal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

Fixes an issue where iOS users scanning a gateway pairing QR could have the scanner dismiss at the wrong time, lose the trust/approval handoff, or crash while VisionKit was still stopping camera capture.

The affected surfaces are the iOS onboarding scanner, Gateway Settings scanner, app/open-url setup-link handling, and post-scan gateway approval handoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scanner now stops VisionKit scanning, queues one typed QR/setup result, dismisses the scanner sheet, and processes pairing only from the sheet dismissal path after a short main-actor settling delay. The final branch also handles setup links delivered during app/onboarding launch by staging UIKit app-delegate URLs through the same gateway setup-link path used by SwiftUI `.onOpenURL`.

This keeps the scanner lifecycle separate from gateway trust UI and avoids re-entering the onboarding/settings presentation stack while VisionKit is still dismissing.

## User Impact

iOS users can pair a gateway by scanning a QR code from onboarding or from Settings without losing the approval flow. After approval, the app reaches Chat and can send/receive messages immediately.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.body:
## Summary

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

1. **Signal outbound adapter** (`src/channels/plugins/outbound/signal.ts`)
   - Updated `sendText()` and `sendMedia()` to pass `replyToId` and `quoteAuthor`

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)
   - Added `replyTo` and `quoteAuthor` to `SignalSendOpts`
   - Converts `replyTo` timestamp into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params
   - Uses `Number()` instead of `parseInt()` for strict timestamp validation
   - Guards group quotes: skips quoting when `quoteAuthor` is missing (avoids silent signal-cli failures)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)
   - `trackReplyConsumption` pattern for bestEffort partial-failure handling
   - `sendPayload` branch routes through quote gating
   - Reply metadata consumed only after successful send
   - Per-payload explicit `replyToId` preserved independently of inherited reply

4. **Event handler — outbound** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - `resolveQuotedAuthor()` with LRU cache for group quote-author resolution
   - Only falls back to current sender for `[[reply_to_current]]`, not explicit `[[reply_to:<id>]]`

### Inbound Changes (user → agent)

5. **Expanded quote types** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.types.ts`)
   - `SignalQuote` type captures full signal-cli payload: `id`, `author`, `authorNumber`, `authorUuid`, `text`, `mentions`, `attachments`, `textStyles`
   - New `SignalQuotedAttachment`, `SignalTextStyle`, `SignalReplyTarget` types

6. **Quote context module** (`src/signal/monitor/quote-context.ts` — NEW)
   - `describeSignalReplyTarget()` extracts structured quote context from inbound messages
   - `normalizeSignalQuoteId()` validates quote timestamps with strict `Number()` parsing
   - Author resolution cascade: `authorNumber` → `authorUuid` → `author` → LRU cache fallback
   - Handles mentions in quoted text, media attachment placeholders, edge cases

7. **Structured context surfacing** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - Inbound quotes surfaced as `ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`, `ReplyToSender`, `ReplyToIsQuote`
   - Both the user message AND the quoted text are preserved
   - Group and DM quote handling unified

### Tests

- Comprehensive test suite for outbound quote mechanics
- New `event-handler.inbound-contract.test.ts` for inbound quote contract tests
- Refactored `event-handler.quote.test.ts` with edge case coverage
- All tests passing

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Outbound Signal quote-reply parameters were never translated into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params, and inbound user quote-replies were dropped or only surfaced as fallback body text. After this fix, `resolveSignalQuoteMetadata` produces the right RPC param shape (and gates out unsafe group quotes), and `describeSignalReplyTarget` returns a structured `SignalReplyTarget` with normalized id, resolved author, body text or media placeholder, and quote kind.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `e3740e0223dba46315f0f568d68a14e4ac72fe59` of branch `fix/signal-quote-reply`. Linux 6.12.67, Node v24.15.0, pnpm-driven monorepo. Patched modules in `extensions/signal/src/reply-quote.ts` and `extensions/signal/src/monitor/quote-context.ts` loaded directly with `tsx` from the working tree, and the built CLI (`pnpm openclaw --version`) reports `OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (e3740e0)` confirming the binary is built from the patched commit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. `pnpm openclaw --version` to confirm the live CLI is built from the patched HEAD.
  2. `node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-pr36630.mts` — driver that loads `extensions/signal/src/reply-quote.ts` and `extensions/signal/src/monitor/quote-context.ts`, then exercises `normalizeSignalQuoteId`, `parseSignalQuoteTimestamp`, `resolveSignalQuoteMetadata` (DM, group, missing author, invalid timestamp), `isSignalGroupTarget`, and `describeSignalReplyTarget` with text-only, image-attachment, missing-author + LRU-resolver, and no-quote payload shapes.
  3. `pnpm test extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.quote.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/reply-delivery.test.ts` — full targeted suites for the changed Signal files.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal capture from running the patched modules in this worktree.

target.title: fix(ui): clear session labels across subscribed clients
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users clearing a session label in one Control UI client would leave other subscribed clients showing the old name until a full session refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway session events now send explicit null tombstones when a label or its derived display name is absent, while preserving explicit rename-flow overrides. The Control UI reconciliation path removes those fields when it receives the tombstones instead of merging stale values forward.

## User Impact

Cleared session labels disappear immediately across subscribed Control UI clients without requiring a refresh.

## Evidence

- Before-fix Testbox regression: `sessions.changed` label assertion received `undefined` instead of the required `null` tombstone.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwrtnmmqnd87cx8wrkhz1fmm`: gateway regression 48/48 passed across both gateway configurations.

target.title: fix #98158: Dashboard fails to load in Chrome v109 because Array.prototype.toSorted is not available
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Chrome v109 does not provide `Array.prototype.toSorted`, and the Control UI can call it during initial dashboard render.
- Solution: Install a focused Control UI entrypoint polyfill for `toSorted` and `toReversed` before `./ui/app.ts` loads.
- What changed: Added `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.ts`, imported it first from `ui/src/main.ts`, and added regression coverage for missing methods, native preservation, and import order.
- What was not changed: dashboard sorting policy, session data shape, gateway API, authentication flow, generated locale bundle, lockfile, and broad ES/Object polyfill surface are unchanged.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Chrome v109 / Windows 7 users can open the dashboard instead of being blocked by an initial-render JavaScript exception.
- **What did NOT change:** No dashboard sorting policy, session data shape, gateway API, authentication flow, generated locale bundle, lockfile, or broad ES/Object polyfill surface changed.
- Fixes #98158

## What Problem This Solves

Chrome v109 / Windows 7 users can hit `toSorted is not a function` while opening the Control UI dashboard. Because the throw happens during app startup, the dashboard/login experience is blocked before the user can connect normally.

## User Impact

Users on the reported legacy browser can open the dashboard instead of being stopped by an initial-render JavaScript exception. Modern browsers keep their native array-copy implementations unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #98168 and #98247 are linked external open PRs for this issue.
- **Related open PR scan:** The linked open PR scan found #98168 and #98247; this body compares both same-issue competing PRs and keeps the scope canonical to the Control UI startup compatibility boundary.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #98168 only replaces the sidebar recent-session `toSorted` call, leaving the same missing-array-copy-method failure class in other Control UI runtime paths. #98247 takes a broad ES polyfill approach, but it changes more global APIs than the Chrome v109 blocker requires and had remote proof/lint failures when this patch was prepared.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** The compatibility boundary belongs at `ui/src/main.ts`, before any Control UI app module can evaluate. This patch installs only the two array-copy methods the UI uses for the reported failure class, preserves native methods, and avoids unrelated `Object`/`Array` global changes.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The proof launches the patched Control UI in a real browser process after removing `toSorted` and `toReversed` before navigation, then observes the entrypoint restores both methods and the page emits no array-copy-method or `TypeError` runtime errors.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Opening the Control UI when array copy methods are absent no longer throws before the dashboard/login screen renders.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux host, Vite dev server, `/usr/bin/google-chrome` driven by Playwright. Before navigation, the browser page set `Array.prototype.toSorted` and `Array.prototype.toReversed` to missing values so the app loaded through the legacy-method path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Started the Control UI dev server and drove system Chrome through the missing-method startup path.

```
pnpm --dir ui dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 58158 --strictPort

Playwright launched /usr/bin/google-chrome, removed Array.prototype.toSorted and
Array.prototype.toReversed before page navigation, then opened:
http://127.0.0.1:58158/
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Browser startup proof from the patched entrypoint:

```
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:58158/chat?session=main",
  "toSortedType": "function",
  "toReversedType": "function",
  "bodySnippet": "OpenClaw\n网关仪表盘\nWebSocket URL\n网关令牌\n密码 (不存储)\n连接\n协议不匹配\n提供的 Control UI 与正在运行的 Gateway 对支持的连接协议不一致。\n使用 openclaw dashboard 重新打开提供的 dashboard，确保 UI 和 Gateway 来自同一安装。\n如果使用 pnpm ui:dev，请基于当前 checkout 重新构建或重启开发 UI。\n更新 OpenClaw 后重启 Gateway，使其提供当前协议。\n原始错误\nControl UI 认证文档\n如何连接\n在主机上启动网关：\nopenclaw gateway run\n获取带令牌的仪表盘 URL：\nopenclaw dashboard\n将 WebSocket URL 和令牌粘贴到上方，或直接打开带令牌的 URL。\n查看文档 →",
  "errors": []
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The page reached the Control UI route, both array copy methods were functions after entrypoint evaluation, and the page produced no `toSorted`, `toReversed`, or `TypeError` runtime errors.
- **What was not tested:** Actual Chrome v109 on Windows 7 was not available. A live Gateway token connection was not used; the browser proof covers the startup/render boundary by removing the missing prototype methods before the Control UI entrypoint runs.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Stale label after follow-up. The author-side lint issue has been fixed on current head `bf62bac1b369d8285663a2f871363dabccd84b21`, CI is green, `proof: sufficient` is present, and the remaining `status: ⏳ waiting on author` label needs ClawSweeper/maintainer refresh rather than another code change.
- **RF-002 / RF-006:** Fixed. The native-preservation assertion now calls `toSorted((a, b) => a - b)` so the type-aware `typescript(require-array-sort-compare)` rule has the required comparator.
- **RF-003:** Addressed. The repair commit touches only `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts`; the runtime polyfill remains narrow and still only defines missing `toSorted`/`toReversed` methods.
- **RF-004 / RF-005:** Addressed. CI `check-lint` failed on the current PR head at `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts:75`; the repair is a one-line test assertion change and does not alter the product direction or runtime scope.
- **RF-007:** Verified with the requested UI test command.
- **RF-008:** Verified with the requested targeted oxlint command for the changed UI files.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts` plus existing `ui/src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts` coverage.
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression test removes `toSorted` and `toReversed`, installs the entrypoint polyfill, checks non-mutating semantics, checks native preservation, and mocks `./ui/app.ts` to prove the fallback is installed before app evaluation.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A single call-site replacement would miss other Control UI array-copy-method usages, while broad ES polyfills would add unrelated behavior. The guardrail is entrypoint-level and limited to the missing array-copy methods.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch adds browser global prototype methods only when the browser lacks native `toSorted` or `toReversed`. Existing native implementations are left intact.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is limited to the Control UI entrypoint and one small polyfill module, with browser startup proof, production build verification, targeted tests, formatting, and lint coverage. The follow-up repair changes only the test assertion that triggered `check-lint`.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: unchanged.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The Control UI source-of-truth startup order in `ui/src/main.ts` imported `./ui/app.ts` before any compatibility setup; because Chrome v109 lacks `Array.prototype.toSorted`, startup/render code could call a missing method before the dashboard/login UI became usable.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix runs at the Control UI source-of-truth entrypoint before downstream app modules evaluate. That changes the startup invariant from "app code may run before array-copy methods exist" to "app code only runs after missing array-copy methods are installed or native methods are preserved."
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings are not symptom masking: the `Array.prototype` type escapes are limited to descriptor access for browser-native methods that may be missing at runtime, the mocked app module returns an empty ESM module only after asserting import order, there are no lint suppressions, no unrelated files, no lockfile changes, and the related open PR scan is addressed in the competition section.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `ui/src/main.ts` owns Control UI startup order; the patch fixes the compatibility contract before dashboard rendering, route setup, or other UI modules can consume array-copy methods.

## Additional verification

```
$ pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-99162/ui test src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #90999.

Users can see contradictory or missing terminal state when `chat.send` dispatch fails around abort/session-lifecycle timing. The bad windows are:

- abort already won, but a later post-dispatch rejection can overwrite the cached terminal result as an error;
- dispatch already failed, but a late `chat.abort` during fallback persistence can mask the real error as an abort;
- a queued followup was accepted, then an explicit abort won before dispatch rejection, and the accepted-followup branch could otherwise bypass the abort-preserve dedupe write;
- session lifecycle interruption after `chat.send` ACK can abort the controller without going through the normal `chat.abort` marker/broadcast path, leaving the client without a terminal `chat` event or keeping the session admission busy after terminal abort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict refresh keeps current `main` session-admission, queued-followup, and dispatch-error lifecycle behavior, then makes terminal ownership explicit:

- if `chat.abort` already recorded the abort marker, preserve the abort terminal result, write the aborted dedupe, release session admission/active-run ownership before fallback persistence, and do not resurrect the run as an error;
- if a followup was already queued and no explicit abort marker owns the run, keep that accepted client run terminal;
- if dispatch/error owns the terminal state, close abortability before any awaited fallback persistence, clear stale abort state, cache the error, and broadcast the error;
- if lifecycle admission interrupts the run, do not treat a bare aborted signal as proof that a terminal abort was already broadcast.

The PR remains limited to `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` and `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`.

## User Impact

`chat.send` clients now receive one stable terminal outcome for these race windows. Same-run retries observe the correct cached terminal result, late abort does not rewrite a real dispatch error, lifecycle-interrupted sends still produce a terminal `chat` event, queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run unless an explicit abort owns the run, and lifecycle operations are not held behind unrelated fallback transcript persistence after a terminal abort.

Related: #84176 and #84306.

## Evidence

Candidate head / proof head: `5c2e32c3728d025942fd4d0828a65b15a5f5cf8f`

Green upstream base merged for this branch refresh: `8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916` (`openclaw/openclaw` `main`, CI run `28737444248` succeeded). The merge-tree against that base is clean, and the PR-style diff remains exactly the two Gateway files listed above.

Commands run on the current proof head:

```shell

node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts
git diff --check 8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916...HEAD
git merge-tree --write-tree 8df18050d53298a6fc94740fbc06978719b5e916 HEAD
```


Real Gateway / WebSocket proof was also run on the same proof head with a real OpenClaw Gateway server and real WebSocket RPC client calls (`chat.send` / `chat.abort`). The only controlled boundary is dispatch, using the repository's normal Gateway test seam, so the proof exercises the Gateway server, WebSocket transport, RPC request/response shape, and client-visible `chat` broadcasts without claiming a live provider/model E2E run.

Regression coverage now includes:

- abort-first post-dispatch rejection preserves the terminal timeout/aborted result, serves that cached result to same-run retry, emits no error chat state, and releases lifecycle admission before pending runtime transcript persistence settles;
- queued-followup plus explicit abort still preserves the terminal abort, does not emit a final/error chat state after dispatch rejection, and serves the cached aborted result to same-run retry;
- error-first post-dispatch rejection closes abortability before fallback persistence, makes late `chat.abort` return `aborted:false`, serves cached error during the pending window, emits no aborted chat state, and allows a later retry after error dedupe cleanup;
- lifecycle admission interruption after dispatch start still emits a terminal `chat` error event when no `chat.abort` marker/broadcast exists;
- queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run and keeps the queued turn cached until the followup completes;
- the sibling dispatch-error/session lifecycle suite still passes.

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Changes

- **`src/acp/client.ts`** — replace `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` (1 line)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Object.hasOwn on ACP session notification data

The proof script mirrors the exact `printSessionUpdate` logic and exercises it against realistic ACP `SessionNotification` objects matching the `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` schema (where `sessionUpdate` is a required discriminator const on every `SessionUpdate` union arm).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-99363-printSessionUpdate.mjs
==============================================================
Proof: PR #99363 — Object.hasOwn in printSessionUpdate
==============================================================

📋 Test 1: All ACP sessionUpdate discriminator variants
--------------------------------------------------
  [agentMessageChunk] → matched=true, action="write text to stdout"
  ✅ PASS: agentMessageChunk: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCall] → matched=true, action="log tool read_file (in_progress)"
  ✅ PASS: toolCall: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCallUpdate] → matched=true, action="log update tool_001: completed"
  ✅ PASS: toolCallUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [availableCommandsUpdate] → matched=true, action="log commands: /help /status"
  ✅ PASS: availableCommandsUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [nonSessionUpdate] → matched=false, action="undefined"
  ✅ PASS: nonSessionUpdate: should NOT match (no sessionUpdate)

📋 Test 2: Object.hasOwn vs `in` operator — own-property equivalence
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): true
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true
  ✅ PASS: Both return true for own property

📋 Test 3: Prototype pollution safety — Object.hasOwn advantage
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.prototype.sessionUpdate injected → "agent_message_chunk"
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false ← correctly rejects injected
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true ← incorrectly matches injected
  ✅ PASS: Object.hasOwn correctly REJECTS prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: in operator INCORRECTLY matches prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: Object.prototype.sessionUpdate removed after cleanup

📋 Test 4: Missing property — both operators agree
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               false
  ✅ PASS: Both return false for missing property

==============================================================
Results: 10 passed, 0 failed out of 10 assertions
==============================================================

✅ PROOF PASSED — Object.hasOwn behavior is correct for ACP session updates.

Key findings:
  1. Object.hasOwn and `in` operator behave identically for normal ACP
     session update discriminator properties (all 4 update types pass).
  2. Object.hasOwn correctly rejects non-session-update notifications
     that lack a sessionUpdate own property.
  3. Object.hasOwn provides prototype pollution safety: unlike `in`,
     it does NOT match a prototype-injected sessionUpdate property.
  4. The ACP SDK schema requires sessionUpdate as a required discriminator
     on every SessionUpdate union arm — so in practice both are equivalent,
     but Object.hasOwn is the more defensive, semantically correct choice.
```

target.title: fix(watch): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a `git push` triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) unconditionally kills the current healthy gateway child process and restarts into a broken `dist/`, causing a crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit (37-minute outage).

Fixes [#99603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99603).

## Why This Change Was Made

`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs` sent SIGTERM to the child without verifying build readiness. The fix adds `isBuildReadyForRestart()` which delegates to run-node's canonical readiness contract (`resolveBuildRequirement` + `resolveRuntimePostBuildRequirement` from `run-node.mjs`), but **only defers on hard physical failures** where the child cannot start.

### Hard failures → defer restart
The `dist/` directory is physically broken; the child process cannot start:

| Reason code | Condition |
|-------------|-----------|
| `missing_dist_entry` | `dist/entry.js` does not exist (mid-rebuild) |
| `missing_bundled_plugin_dist_entry` | Required bundled plugin output missing |
| `missing_private_qa_dist` | Private QA dist entries missing |
| `missing_runtime_postbuild_output` | Required runtime postbuild outputs missing |

### Soft staleness → allow restart (preserves normal gateway:watch behavior)
The `dist/` directory exists and is usable. Run-node will rebuild on the next start:

| Reason code | Condition |
|-------------|-----------|
| `missing_build_stamp` | Build stamp file missing but `dist/entry.js` exists |
| `git_head_changed` | Git HEAD changed (`git pull`) |
| `dirty_watched_tree` | Uncommitted source changes |
| `config_newer` | Config file newer than build stamp |
| `build_stamp_missing_head` | Build stamp exists but lacks HEAD field |
| `source_mtime_newer` | Source file mtime newer than build stamp |

**Masked missing-entry detection**: `resolveBuildRequirement` checks `missing_build_stamp` before `missing_dist_entry`. When both stamp and entry are absent the reason is `missing_build_stamp` (soft staleness) but `dist/entry.js` is also gone. A direct `existsSync` check in the `missing_build_stamp` branch catches this masked case and defers correctly.

**Deferral mechanism**: When a hard failure is detected, the watcher polls every 200ms until the build is ready. A **5-minute timeout** prevents infinite polling — the current process keeps running and a future file change retries.

**Child-exit bounded recovery**: If the child exits during deferral, the exit handler also waits for readiness with a 5-min timeout, then falls back to `startRunner()`.

**Environment consistency**: The watcher's `deps.env` is passed into readiness checks, matching the child runner's `OPENCLAW_FORCE_BUILD` / `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA` flags.

**Test mode**: Both guards skip when `OPENCLAW_WATCH_MODE=test` to preserve existing test isolation.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Source changes during mid-rebuild → watcher kills healthy gateway → new child cannot start → crash-loop → systemd gives up → 37-min outage
- **After**: Only defers on hard failures. Normal source/config edits restart immediately (run-node rebuilds on start). Mid-rebuild waits for `dist/entry.js` → safe restart.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (29/29 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/watch-node.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Test coverage:
- **3 hard-failure tests** (`missing_dist_entry`, `missing_bundled_plugin_dist_entry`, `missing_private_qa_dist`) — verifies child is NOT killed
- **6 soft-staleness tests** (`missing_build_stamp`, `git_head_changed`, `dirty_watched_tree`, `config_newer`, `build_stamp_missing_head`, `source_mtime_newer`) — verifies child IS killed normally (run-node will rebuild)
- **1 masked missing-entry test** (both stamp and entry absent → `missing_build_stamp` reason but entry also gone) — verifies direct entry check defers
- **1 runtime hard-failure test** (`missing_runtime_postbuild_output`) — defer
- **1 clean contract test** — normal kill+restart
- **1 timeout test** — gives up after 5 min, process stays alive
- **1 child-exit deferral test** — defers on hard failure, recovers when ready

### Real Machine Gateway:Watch Proof

**Environment**: Linux x64, Node v22.19.0,host `LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra`

```
============================================================
  Issue #99603 — Real Machine Verification
============================================================

Host:     LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra
Kernel:   4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
Node:     v22.19.0

=== Start gateway:watch ===
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 node scripts/watch-node.mjs gateway
watcher PID: 268228

=== Process health ===
$ ps -p 268228 -o pid,stat,etime,comm --no-headers
 268228 Sl 01:15 node                    ← watcher healthy
$ ps -p 268590 -o pid,stat,etime,comm --no-headers
 268590 Sl 01:14 node                    ← child healthy

============================================================
  Test 1: Normal source edit (soft staleness → no defer)
============================================================
$ touch src/entry.ts
→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=true reason=source_mtime_newer
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: soft staleness → allow restart
→ child killed normally, run-node rebuilds ✅

============================================================
  Test 2: Both stamp + entry missing (masked → defer)
============================================================
$ rm dist/.buildstamp && rm dist/entry.js
$ touch src/entry.ts

--- watcher output ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.

→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=true reason=missing_build_stamp
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: missing_build_stamp + direct entry check
→ entry.js absent → hard failure → defer ✅

This confirms: when both stamp and entry are missing, the masked
missing_dist_entry case is caught by the direct existsSync check
in the missing_build_stamp branch, preventing the crash.

============================================================
  Test 3: Restore entry + stamp → recovery
============================================================
$ git checkout -- src/entry.ts
$ cp /tmp/e.js dist/entry.js && cp /tmp/s.json dist/.buildstamp

--- watcher output ---
[openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.

→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=false reason=clean
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: true → safe restart ✅

============================================================
  Full watcher log
============================================================
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: git_head_changed).
  [openclaw] Building bundled plugin assets.
  [openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
  [openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
  [openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.
  [openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.
  [openclaw] Syncing runtime artifacts (build_stamp_newer).

--- MAIN branch (no fix) comparison ---
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: missing_dist_entry)
  → kills healthy child → crash loop → systemd exhausts restart limit → 37min outage
```

### Verification Summary

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Normal source edit (source_mtime_newer) | No defer, normal restart | ✅ |
| Both stamp + entry missing (masked→missing_build_stamp) | Defer, wait for recovery | ✅ |
| Restore entry + stamp | Detect ready, safe restart | ✅ |
| Watcher alive throughout | Healthy | ✅ |

## Changes

- `scripts/watch-node.mjs`: `isBuildReadyForRestart` delegates to `resolveBuildRequirement` + `resolveRuntimePostBuildRequirement` from run-node.mjs; only defers on hard physical failures with direct entry.js check for masked case; passes `deps.env` for env consistency; 200ms polling + 5-min timeout; child-exit bounded recovery
- `src/infra/watch-node.test.ts`: `vi.mock` run-node exports; 3 hard-failure defer + 6 soft-staleness allow-restart + 1 masked missing-entry + 1 runtime hard-failure + clean + timeout + child-exit = 29 tests total
- `test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts`: +1 suppression allowlist entry

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Three layers in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

### 1. isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)

Comprehensive guard mirroring `run-node`'s `resolveBuildRequirement()`:
- `dist/entry.js` exists
- Build stamp (`dist/.buildstamp`) has valid `builtAt`
- Build stamp git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD
- Config files (`tsdown.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`) mtime not newer than stamp
- Runtime postbuild stamp (`dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp`) exists with `syncedAt >= builtAt`

### 2. Deferred restart polling (1s interval)

When build is not ready, polls every 1s. When build output becomes ready, auto-triggers restart — no manual file change needed.

### 3. Exit handler guard

After SIGTERM/143 child exit, verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop.

## Evidence

### Real gateway:watch proof (current SHA 03954beb)

```
REAL gateway:watch PROOF — SHA: 03954beb32ea
Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Node: v24.13.1

─── 1. isBuildReadyForRestart ───
  ✅ entry.js missing → false
  ✅ no readFileSync (fallback) → true
  ✅ HEAD mismatch (has runtime stamp) → false
  ✅ HEAD match (has runtime stamp) → true

─── 2. Guard points in source ───
  Guard checks: 3 (requestRestart + exit handler + polling)
  Polling reset on settle: yes
  isBuildReadyForRestart exported: yes

─── 3. Unit tests ───
  Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  24 passed (24)

─── 4. Lint ───

```

### Unit tests (24/24 passed)


### Broader regression (91/91 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/run-node.test.ts src/infra/watch-node.test.ts

```

### CI status

All checks-node-compact-small-* pass. Lint + type-check clean.

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
- **Partial mitigation** — prevents crash-loop; issue #99603 should remain open for transactional restart (build-then-swap)

- Offer migration from supported agent environments before separate model setup, keep accepted plugin installs managed, and leave cancelled imports retryable.

target.title: fix: support baseURL alias in memory embedding provider config resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When users configure `models.providers.openai.baseURL` (capital `URL`) for a local or OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint, the strict provider schema used to reject/drop that alias instead of exposing the canonical `baseUrl` field downstream.

Fixes #93396.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` | Accept `models.providers.*.baseURL`, normalize it to canonical `baseUrl`, delete the alias before downstream code reads the provider config, and reject configs that set both spellings. |
| `src/config/schema.hints.ts` | Walk Zod pipes while collecting schema hint paths so transformed provider schemas keep sensitive URL metadata for `models.providers.*.baseUrl` and its `baseURL` alias. |
| `src/config/schema.test.ts` | Covers `baseURL` normalization, alias deletion, duplicate-spelling rejection, and sensitive URL metadata on the alias path. |
| `src/config/schema.hints.test.ts` | Covers discovery of the `models.providers.*.baseURL` sensitive URL hint path. |
| `src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts` | Covers redacting embedded credentials from provider `baseURL` aliases in config snapshots. |
| `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts` | Treats `models.providers.*.baseURL` as a sensitive URL config path alongside `baseUrl`. |
| `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts` | Covers the alias in the shared sensitive URL path predicate. |
| `src/agents/memory-search.ts` | Keeps the direct built-in memory adapter when one exists. The OpenAI memory adapter already reads canonical provider `baseUrl`, so routing should stay on the existing adapter instead of becoming an unconfigured provider. |
| `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` | Strengthens the `baseURL` coverage so schema-normalized config must still resolve the built-in OpenAI memory adapter and its default model. |

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `models.providers.openai.baseURL` is accepted by the production schema, normalized to `baseUrl`, then used by the real OpenAI memory embedding path to call the configured `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.

**Exact commands run after fix:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/schema.hints.test.ts src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts
git diff --check
PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/schema.hints.test.ts src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/schema.hints.test.ts src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.test.ts src/agents/memory-search.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.hints.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
node --import tsx /Users/yangjiajun/projects/auto-pr/workspace/openclaw/outputs/issue-93396-pr-93505/verify-baseurl-endpoint.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence:**

```text
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 4.93s

git diff --check: passed
OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256
oxfmt: All matched files use the correct format.
oxlint: passed
tsgo core: passed
tsgo core-test: passed

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 7.30s

src/config/schema.test.ts: 57 passed
src/agents/memory-search.test.ts: 37 passed

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 9.41s

src/config/schema.hints.test.ts: 11 passed

pnpm check:test-types: passed
```

The endpoint proof starts a local HTTP server, parses config through `OpenClawSchema`, registers the real OpenAI memory adapter, resolves memory search config, and calls `embedBatch`.

```json
{
  "schemaDeletedBaseURLAlias": true,
  "resolvedProvider": "openai",
  "resolvedModel": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "adapterProviderId": "openai",
  "request": {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "/v1/embeddings",
    "authorization": "Bearer <redacted>",
    "contentType": "application/json",
    "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
    "inputCount": 2
  },
  "vectors": [
    [0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
    [1.1, 1.2, 1.3]
  ]
}
```

**Observed result:** The alias is removed after schema normalization, duplicate `baseUrl`/`baseURL` config is rejected, the alias carries the same sensitive URL metadata as `baseUrl`, memory search resolves the OpenAI built-in adapter with `text-embedding-3-small`, and the real embedding request hits the configured `/v1/embeddings` route rather than falling back to an unconfigured path.

target.title: fix(ui): avoid fallback main session parent in Control UI
target.body:
Closes #93422

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI typed chat commands did not consistently create or rename sessions with the user-provided visible name. `/new Research Plan` could lose the intended name while creating or resetting a chat, and `/label <name>` was not reliably handled as a local Control UI session command.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes Control UI session naming through the existing gateway `label` contract instead of adding a second writable naming field. The `/new <name>` slash-command flow now passes the typed label through the real `ChatPage` adapter into `sessions.create`, including the `session.dmScope='main'` reset-in-place path, and `/label <name>` patches the active session label. New-chat parent selection still avoids unknown, synthetic, and fallback main rows so session lineage stays tied to persisted sessions only.

The generated Swift protocol model is updated from the gateway schema after removing the proposed `displayName` create/patch inputs. The change intentionally stays within session naming and parent-selection behavior; it does not change model routing, auth, archive/pin semantics, or transcript storage format.

## User Impact

Users can create a named chat from the Control UI with `/new Research Plan` and see that label persist through the gateway session store and session list. Users can also rename the current chat with `/label <name>` without waiting for an active run to finish.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): thinking-enabled Anthropic sessions fail with "Invalid signature" after tool loops
target.body:
Closes #99382

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where extended-thinking Anthropic sessions would fail with a 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block` and abort the turn after longer tool-use loops, with no compaction involved. The affected surface is Anthropic native message replay — both the SDK converter and the transport converter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Anthropic ignores past-turn thinking blocks for generation but still validates their signatures. With thinking enabled, both converters replayed every signed thinking block from completed turns, so any divergence between the reconstructed history and what the provider originally signed was rejected.

This scopes thinking replay instead of replaying unconditionally:

- `fable5` contracts keep full replay (unchanged).
- Thinking-enabled non-`fable5` models replay only the current turn — messages at or after the latest user message, plus the active tool-use turn whose thinking Anthropic requires for continuation.
- Thinking-disabled requests keep the existing tool-turn-only behavior.

Past-turn thinking is dropped before the payload is built, with one structured diagnostic per request for observability. Non-goal: this does not change compaction handling; the boundaryless-compaction path is #98527.

## Related PR Matrix

- #99383: canonical no-compaction completed-turn native Anthropic replay-policy fix. This PR owns the SDK and managed transport request builders.
- #94649: complementary recovery-side terminal-result handling; not a create-side replay prevention replacement.
- #99772 / #99620: separate NO_REPLY/custom-separator merge-shape fix (`cannot be modified`); not the completed-turn invalid-signature replay class fixed here.
- #100149: broader session-history sanitizer candidate; it changes more signed-thinking surfaces and currently has a ClawSweeper P1 replay-safe tool ID preservation blocker.
- #95819: Bedrock sibling fix; not the native Anthropic path fixed here.
- #94493 / #98831 / #99437: closed or partial-overlap attempts in the same signed-thinking replay cluster, superseded here by the scoped helper plus live proof.

## Scope Boundary

This PR fixes the completed-turn stale signed-thinking replay class:

- Failure shape: completed prior assistant thinking is replayed into a later Anthropic request.
- Provider error: HTTP 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block`.
- Fix shape: non-`fable5` thinking-enabled requests replay only current-turn thinking, while preserving active tool-use thinking.
- Covered surfaces: SDK Anthropic converter and managed Anthropic transport.

This PR does not claim to fix the NO_REPLY/custom-separator merge class from #99620/#99772:

- Failure shape: silent/custom cleanup leaves adjacent assistant messages that merge into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`.
- Provider error: HTTP 400 `thinking or redacted_thinking blocks ... cannot be modified`.
- Reason: that class is a transcript-shape merge bug, not the completed-turn invalid-signature replay bug fixed here.

## User Impact

Extended-thinking Anthropic sessions continue past longer tool loops without Invalid-signature rejections. No behavior change for `fable5` replay, thinking-disabled requests, or the in-flight tool-use turn.

## Proof Matrix

| Case | Failure / risk | PR behavior | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Completed prior thinking replay | Anthropic rejects raw replay with 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block` | Past-turn thinking dropped; prior `tool_use` preserved; provider returns 200 | Covered by #99383 |
| Active tool-use continuation | Current active tool-use thinking must remain replayable | Preserved | Covered by #99383 |
| `fable5` replay contract | Full thinking replay must remain unchanged | Preserved | Covered by #99383 |
| SDK + managed transport parity | Both Anthropic builders must share the same replay invariant | Targeted tests cover both | Covered by #99383 |
| NO_REPLY merge into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]` | Anthropic rejects with `cannot be modified` | Not claimed here | Covered separately by #99620/#99772 |

## Evidence

- AI-assisted: implemented with an AI coding agent. I reviewed the code, tests, and final diff and understand the change.
- New targeted tests (SDK + transport converters): completed-turn thinking is dropped when thinking is enabled on non-`fable5` models, the in-flight parallel tool-use turn's thinking is preserved, and `fable5` still replays full thinking.
- Rebased refresh on PR head `b9a6d2829ec1fd9cb9a90ee9ef8c584b3af0a64e` (2026-07-05):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts` — 47 tests passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — 89 tests passed.

- Earlier branch checks before the rebase refresh:

  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — 84 tests passed.
  - `oxlint` reported 0 warnings / 0 errors on the changed files.

## Live Anthropic Provider Proof

Live Anthropic provider proof on earlier PR head `aa76f779da88e17d34d7ae3826ba218b4e71b413` (2026-07-03 16:30 KST):

target.title: fix(google): bound Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

```text
stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > caps an oversized body streamed chunked over real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] oversized path: cap=16777216 reported=16842704 server_total=18874368

stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] normal path: cap=16777216 returned=45 body="{\"access_token\":\"loopback\",\"expires_in\":3600}"
```

Targeted unit proof: the new tests drive the production `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders` -> `refreshGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAccessToken` -> `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` path with real `Response` streams passed through an injected `fetchImpl`. They cover the normal authorized_user refresh case and the oversized streamed refresh body case that previously relied on unbounded `arrayBuffer()`.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http fetchWithTimeout body byte cap > caps oversized response body at 16 MiB with labeled overflow error
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http fetchWithTimeout body byte cap > returns a Response for normal-size bodies
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > caps an oversized body streamed chunked over real wire
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts > vertex-adc OAuth token response bounds > parses a normal token refresh response
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts > vertex-adc OAuth token response bounds > rejects oversized token refresh bodies instead of buffering the whole stream

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.15s
```

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/google/oauth.http.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

```text
branch: fix/google-bound-vertex-oauth-responses

autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.74)
```

Notes for reviewers:

- The 16 MiB cap matches the existing Google OAuth HTTP helper in `oauth.http.ts`. Legitimate ADC token responses are far smaller; the cap is a fail-closed bound against unbounded wire reads, not a product limit change.
- This PR intentionally does not include the gzip `maxOutputLength` hardening present in #98507. If maintainers prefer one combined fix, that sibling PR is the broader option; this one is the minimal shared-cap alignment for the ADC refresh read site.
- This PR does not add or migrate persistent state.

AI-assisted: built with Codex. I understand the change: it replaces the unbounded Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh `arrayBuffer()` read with the shared 16 MiB bounded response reader and adds focused regression tests for normal and oversized streamed refresh bodies.

target.title: fix: avoid splitting surrogate pairs in node-host truncateOutput
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `truncateOutput` in the node-host invoke path uses raw `String.prototype.slice` for tail truncation. When the cut point falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extension B+), the result string starts with a lone low surrogate and `isWellFormed()` returns `false`. Ill-formed Unicode can be rejected by strict UTF-8 encoders, JSON transports, and database drivers.

**Solution**: Replace the raw `raw.slice(raw.length - maxChars)` with the existing `sliceUtf16Safe(raw, raw.length - maxChars)` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. This helper is already tested and used in 30+ files across the repository.

What changed: `src/node-host/invoke.ts` — one call-site in `truncateOutput` (+ import). `src/node-host/invoke.test.ts` — four new unit tests.

What did NOT change: Public API, truncation threshold semantics, output format, any other exec-output path.

Fixes #99981

## Root Cause

`String.prototype.slice` operates on UTF-16 code units without surrogate-pair awareness. One emoji or supplementary-plane character occupies 2 code units (a surrogate pair). Slicing between them splits the pair, producing an ill-formed string.

```
$ node -e "console.log('😀'.repeat(10).slice(15).isWellFormed())"
false
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Tail-truncated exec output becomes ill-formed Unicode when the cut lands inside a surrogate pair.

Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.20.0, openclaw main @ c64a306f90.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```
node --import tsx -e "
const { truncateOutput } = require('./src/node-host/invoke.ts');
const r1 = truncateOutput('hello world', 5);
console.log('ASCII:', r1.text);
const r2 = truncateOutput('😀'.repeat(10), 5);
const tail = r2.text.replace('... (truncated) ', '');
console.log('emoji wellFormed:', tail.isWellFormed());
console.log('emoji tail:', JSON.stringify(tail));
"
```

After-fix evidence:
```
ASCII: ... (truncated) world
emoji wellFormed: true
emoji tail: "😀😀"
```

Observed result after the fix: ASCII truncation unchanged. Emoji tail is well-formed Unicode (`isWellFormed() === true`). Unit tests: 6 passed, 3 skipped (platform-conditional), 0 failed.

What was not tested: Full gateway end-to-end with a real node-host sending emoji-laden exec output. The fix is a pure string-safety change — `sliceUtf16Safe` has comprehensive surrogate-pair tests in its own package.

## Risk checklist

- [x] merge-risk: low — single call-site replacement, no control-flow or API change
- [x] Diff ≤ 100 lines (+41/-3 in 2 files)
- [x] No lockfile or CHANGELOG changes
- [x] Reuses existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper (self-tested), no new dependencies
- [x] 4 new unit tests covering surrogate pair, ASCII, short-text scenarios
- [x] No cross-module impact — `truncateOutput` only called by `buildExecEventPayload`
